slides.title: My Phone Number and Address

runs.t: I can say a phone number.
I can ask: What's your address?
I can use my, your, his, her.
I can fill out a simple form.

slides.notes:
Point to each line and read it. Learners repeat. Click to show the next goal.
Say: "Tonight: phone numbers, addresses, and a form." Mime writing on a form.
Point to 13 and 30 on the board: "Thirteen... thirty. We practice this at 7:15."
Say: "At 7:25 we do the Progress Check."

slides.title: Today's Goals

shapes.name: Name tag
shapes.alt: A form with the CITY line highlighted

slides.notes:
Before class, write on the board: Where are you from? What city? Where is he / she from? Is he / she from ___?
Model with one learner: "Where are you from?" "Guatemala." "What city?" "Antigua." Then point to another learner: "Where is she from?" "She's from Mexico."
Click to show the A line, then the B line. Pairs: A asks, B answers. Then ask about a classmate. Switch. Then find a new partner.
Help lines: Can you repeat, please? How do you spell it?
Last 3 minutes: partners show each other last week's homework. Look at item 2 (am / is / are).
If behind: one partner only.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Step 1 Hello + Review; Student Page 1).

runs.t: Model it. Check it. Then go.

slides.notes:
Point to each word and do the action: listen (hand to ear), repeat, point, circle, write, partner, group. Learners copy you.
Say: "Model it. Check it. Then go." Do one example with a learner. Ask: "Listen or write?" Then everyone starts.
Privacy: say "This is practice. You don't need your real phone number or address." Use practice numbers 555-0100 to 555-0199 and the practice ID cards.
Pairs: turn to a neighbor. With an odd number, make one group of 3.

runs.t: Ana is at a clinic. She's a new patient.

slides.notes:
Say: "This is Ana. She's at a clinic. She's a new patient. The receptionist asks: What's your phone number? What's your address?" Point to the form (Task B).
Click to show each listen: Listen 1 = Task A (circle). Listen 2 = Task B (the form). Listen 3 = Task C (check what Ana writes).
The audio L1_L3_listening.mp3 (about 1:05) plays the conversation once. Press play again for the next listen. Voices: Narrator, Receptionist, Ana.
Say it (2 min): the class repeats each line twice. Then pairs ask and answer with a practice number.
No speaker? Read the script with a volunteer. Read numbers slowly, in groups: five-five-five... oh-one-four-two.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Step 3 Listening + Say it; Listening script); audio/README.md.

slides.title: What's your phone number?

shapes.name: Picture letter
shapes.alt: Signature line with the name Ana Ruiz

slides.notes:
This is the key point. Point to a man: "his phone number." Point to a woman: "her phone number."
Point to yourself: "my." To a learner: "your." To the class and you: "our class." To two learners: "their city."
Write on the board: he → his. she → her. Click to show the examples.
The big mistake this week: his and her. The word depends on the person, not the thing. Correct by pointing to the person: "Carlos... his."
Check questions: point to a man: "What's ___ name?" (his). To a woman (her). "I'm Ana. ___ last name is Ruiz." (My)
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Step 4 Grammar Q&A, Box 2; Grammar Box 2; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Is your phone number 555-0124?

slides.notes:
Read the left side. Click to show the right side. The class reads it.
Say the groups with a small stop: 555 ... 0142. 0 is usually "oh."
Street numbers are usually in pairs: 210 = two-ten, 1850 = eighteen-fifty. The number comes before the street name: 210 Pine Street (not Pine Street 210).
Pair drill (3–4 min): A asks about a person (Ana, Carlos); B answers. Then switch. If behind, skip the pair drill; it becomes homework.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Step 4 Grammar Q&A, Box 4; Grammar Box 4; Questions and answers; Teacher notes).

slides.notes:
Learners write one word in each line. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 My, 2 His, 3 Her, 4 your, 5 Her.
Look at the person: a man → his (Carlos). A woman → her (Ana, Kim).
Pair drill: A asks "What's his phone number?" B answers from the line.

shapes.name: Picture classmates
shapes.alt: Identification card with the label ID

slides.notes:
Give half the class the Student A page and half the Student B page. Partners don't show their pages. With an odd number, two Bs share one A.
Model with one learner (you are A): "What's your first name?" "Marco." "How do you spell your last name?" "S-I-L-V-A." "What's your phone number?" "555-0163." "Can you repeat, please?"
Part 1 (5 min): A asks and writes B's information. Then B asks and writes A's.
Part 2 (2 min): partners show their pages and check. Fix mistakes together.
Part 3 (2 min): join another pair. Say 2 sentences: "Her name is Rosa Diaz. Her phone number is 555-0187." / "His address is 1850 Lake Avenue."
Baseline snapshot: while pairs work, call the last learners you haven't checked. If behind: skip Part 3.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Step 5 Talk Time; Talk Time Student A and Student B).

slides.title: Talk Time

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says a phone number (a practice number is fine: "My phone number is 555-01__.") or writes one sentence with his or her ("Her phone number is 555-0187."). Copying is fine.
Homework: open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first two lines of the form). Point to each instruction.
Homework items: 1 fill out the form in CAPITAL letters and sign (own information or the practice ID card); 2 write my, his, her, our, or their; 3 write the number; 4 say a phone number 3 times, in groups; 5 review: write about you.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Step 6 Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework).

slides.title: Before You Go

slides.notes:
See it (1 min): point to 20, 30, 40... 100 on the left and say each one. Learners repeat.
Say it (3 min): say each pair 3 times: "thir-TEEN... THIR-ty." Click to show the -ty side. Clap on the strong part. -teen is long and strong at the end; -ty is short and strong at the start.
Learners show 1 finger + 3 for 13, and 3 fingers + a circle (0) for 30. The page also has 17 / 70 (seven-TEEN, SEV-en-ty) and 18 / 80 (eigh-TEEN, EIGH-ty).
Quick check (1 min): say 14 or 40, 15 or 50... Learners point.
When you hear a mix-up, ask: "One-three or three-zero?" and write both on the board.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Letters & Numbers step; Student Pages: Letters & Numbers A and -teen or -ty?; Teacher notes).
slides.title: -teen or -ty?

slides.notes:
Say each number 2 times: 1 thirty, 2 fourteen, 3 fifty, 4 sixteen, 5 ninety. Learners circle.
Pairs compare. Then click 5 times to show the answers: 30, 14, 50, 16, 90.
Task C: read 2 practice phone numbers in groups, 2 times each: 555-0163 (five-five-five, oh-one-six-three) and 555-0118 (five-five-five, oh-one-one-eight). Learners write them.
Task D: learners copy the card (Rosa Diaz, 46 Oak Street, Riverside) into the form in CAPITAL letters: ROSA, DIAZ, 46 OAK STREET, RIVERSIDE.
Partners: A says a practice phone number (555-01__), B writes it. Switch. Learners who can't write yet say the numbers and point; in Task D they copy only the first and last name.
If behind: do Tasks A and B only.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Letters & Numbers step; Student Pages: Letters & Numbers B, C, D; Answer key).
slides.title: Numbers: Task B

slides.notes:
Part A: read the 5 numbers slowly, 2 times each: 13, 40, 15, 70, 80. Learners circle.
Part B: learners match the question and the answer. Click to show the answers: 1 b, 2 d, 3 a, 4 c.
Part C (write my, his, or her): 1 His, 2 Her, 3 My.
Part D: read each "I can..." line and point to the faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Collect the pages. If behind, do it in Week 4 at 6:00.
Source: Level1_Lesson3.md (Progress Check step; Student Pages: Progress Check; Answer key).
